answer: A bonded identity registry makes every agent lock stake before transacting. The deposit sits in a contract, like fossils in shale, until a challenge window passes and bad actors get slashed. An attacker must fund each identity separately, so fakes never reach zero cost. The network builds a trellis of reputation atop the bond, rewarding only identities surviving multiple disputes. New agents start at the lowest tier, like yarrow sprouting before anchoring, capped on throughput regardless of clones. Proven agents climb the trellis for capacity, making sybil floods costly.
